title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck tries to axiomatise a tame topology (the programme of the Esquisse, §5). A 'figure' is a tamely stratified piece of a space. Each figure F is identified with a finite set of elementary figures; an elementary figure is roughly the closure of an open stratum with its induced stratification. This set lies in a universe F_el, carrying several structures numbered (1), (2), (3), ...: (1) the order ≤ ('inclusion'), and (3) a compatibility relation.

Page 14 introduced a finer relation, 'refinement': F' ≪ F if every open stratum of F' lies in an (unique) open stratum of F. Then |F'| ⊂ |F|, and refinement is coarser than inclusion (inclusion = every open stratum of F' is an open stratum of F). Page 14 also noted that refinement of figures reduces to refinement of their elementary pieces.

Page 15 does the following.
(i) Provisional definition: F' is a subdivision of F iff F' refines F and has the same support. Grothendieck flags ("cf plus bas") that this should be equivalent to F' being maximal (for ≤ / ⊂) among the refinements of F.
(ii) This gives two distinct kinds of structure. Structure (5): an order ≪ on F_el ('refinement'), implied by ≤. For figures F, F' ⊂ F_el, 'F refines F'' means: for every x ∈ F there is x' ∈ F' with x ≪ x'.
(iii) Key axiom: for x, x' ∈ F_el, x ≤ x' iff {x, x'} is compatible and x ≪ x'. Consequence: F ≤ F' iff F, F' are compatible and F ≪ F'. The margin draws the moral that structures (3) (compatibility) and (5) (refinement) together determine structure (1) (inclusion).
(iv) Final definition: F' is a subdivision of F if it is a refinement of F and is maximal for ⊂ among the refinements of F.

Page 16 then sets out to prove that a maximal refinement has full support |F'| = |F|. To do so he extends a refinement F' of F by adding the connected components of U_i \ (U_i ∩ |F'|) as new strata, and identifies the frontier condition for these components as a genuine problem about the complement of a stratified subset in a tame manifold.

Modern reading: this is the order theory of the poset of tame (o-minimal / semialgebraic) stratified subsets:
- face/sub-stratification order,
- refinement order,
- compatibility (existence of a common stratification),
- subdivision = refinement with full support.
The characterisation 'inclusion = compatible + refinement' is elementary: compatible strata are equal or disjoint, so containment forces equality.
errors: Slip in line 2: 'elle raffine F'' should read 'elle raffine F'.
Mixed use of ≤ and ⊂ for the maximality condition defining subdivision (first written with ≤, final definition with ⊂); presumably the same inclusion order (1).

The equivalence 'maximal refinement ⇔ same support' is asserted but not proved on this page. Page 16 shows it needs a nontrivial frontier/stratification argument; in the o-minimal setting it follows from cell decomposition / existence of compatible stratifications.

The precise definitions of 'compatible' and of elementary figure come from earlier pages, so the axiom x ≤ x' ⇔ (compatible ∧ x ≪ x') cannot be checked fully here. Under the natural reading it is correct.

ideas.what: Refinement order on stratified figures and on their elementary pieces; figure-level refinement defined pointwise (∀x∈F ∃x'∈F' with x≪x')
ideas.modern_name: refinement of stratifications / partitions (o-minimal or semialgebraic)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Whitney, Thom, Mather; Łojasiewicz; o-minimal: van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 sketches tame topology but not this formalism

ideas.what: Inclusion order recovered from compatibility + refinement: x ≤ x' ⇔ {x,x'} compatible and x ≪ x'; hence F ≤ F' ⇔ compatible and F ≪ F'
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic poset-of-strata structure; face order vs refinement order

ideas.what: Subdivision defined as a ⊂-maximal refinement, claimed equivalent to a refinement with the same support
ideas.modern_name: subdivision of a stratification / cell decomposition refinement
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL topology; o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries)

missed.claim: An attempt to axiomatise tame topology order-theoretically. A universe of elementary figures carries three interlocking relations (inclusion, compatibility, refinement) and subdivision is defined intrinsically as maximal refinement. This is a different route from the o-minimal (definable-sets) axiomatics that the literature actually took. The programme is left incomplete; the needed full-support lemma becomes an 'interesting problem' on the next page.
missed.quote: Donc les structures (3) et (5) impliquent structure (1)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mild interest for anyone seeking a combinatorial or poset-theoretic axiomatisation of tame/stratified spaces, e.g. exit-path categories or posets of strata in stratified homotopy theory. Mathematically elementary, though; the o-minimal framework already supplies the needed results.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary order-theoretic bookkeeping for stratified figures. It is historically interesting as a glimpse of Grothendieck's own attempted axiomatics of tame topology, but it contains no result a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 'elle raffine F' [?]' reads 'elle raffine F' (with a prime) in the hand, but mathematically should be F.
Lines 3–4 read roughly: 'et si elle a même support. Mais (cf plus bas) cela signifie aussi que F' est maximale pour la relation ≤ parmi les figures qui raffinent F.'
Margin: 'Donc les structures ③ et ⑤ impliquent structure ①'.
